en: A pair of small speakers worn over or in the ears to listen to music or other sounds privately.
ex: He listens to music on his headphones on the train.
他在火車上用耳機聽音樂。

en: A severe lack of food that can cause suffering and death.
ex: Thousands of people died of starvation during the famine.
饑荒期間有數千人餓死。

en: The fastest speed at which a horse can run; or to run or ride very fast.
ex: The horses galloped across the open field.
馬匹飛奔穿過開闊的原野。

en: A cheap place to stay, especially for young travelers, with shared rooms and facilities.
ex: We stayed in a youth hostel to save money on our trip.
我們住青年旅館，以節省旅費。

en: A skin condition, common among teenagers, that causes red spots on the face.
ex: Many teenagers suffer from acne.
許多青少年受青春痘所困擾。

en: A serious attempt to do something; or to try very hard to do something.
ex: We will endeavor to answer all your questions.
我們會盡力回答你所有的問題。

en: To walk quietly on your toes so that no one hears you; or the end of your toes.
ex: She tiptoed into the room so she wouldn't wake the baby.
她躡手躡腳地走進房間，免得吵醒寶寶。

en: To control and use something, especially natural power or resources; or the set of straps used on a horse or for safety.
ex: Engineers are trying to harness the energy of the waves.
工程師們正試圖利用海浪的能量。

en: A place where roads or lines cross; or a journey across water or land.
ex: Always look both ways at a pedestrian crossing.
在行人穿越道一定要左右看。

en: A place where historical records are kept; or to save documents or data for long-term storage.
ex: The old photographs are kept in the city archive.
那些老照片存放在市立檔案館裡。

en: The name that you share with other members of your family, usually the last part of your full name.
ex: Please write your surname in capital letters.
請用大寫字母寫下你的姓。

en: To prove that a statement or idea is wrong; or to say something is not true.
ex: The scientist refuted the theory with clear evidence.
科學家以明確的證據駁倒了這個理論。

en: Always; every time, without exception.
ex: He is invariably late for meetings.
他開會總是遲到。

en: Including all or nearly everything; or a type of school that teaches students of all abilities.
ex: The book gives a comprehensive overview of the subject.
這本書對該主題做了全面的概述。

en: The process of joining separate parts or countries into one.
ex: The unification of the two companies took two years.
這兩家公司的合併花了兩年。

en: A person who tells a story, or whose voice explains what is happening in a film or documentary.
ex: The narrator of the story is a young boy.
這個故事的敘述者是個小男孩。

en: A wide street in a city, often with trees along both sides.
ex: They strolled along the tree-lined boulevard.
他們沿著林蔭大道散步。

en: A thick, oily substance, such as the fat from cooked meat; or to put oil on something.
ex: He put some grease on the wheels of the bicycle.
他在腳踏車的輪子上塗了一些潤滑油。

en: A book with a soft paper cover, cheaper than a hardback.
ex: I bought a paperback copy of the novel for the trip.
我買了這本小說的平裝版帶去旅行。

en: The unfair and cruel treatment of a group of people, often by a government.
ex: The people rose up against years of oppression.
人民起來反抗多年的壓迫。

en: Moving or leading to a lower place or level.
ex: Share prices took a sharp downward turn.
股價急轉直下。

en: Very informal words and phrases used in everyday speech, often by a particular group.
ex: The word "cool" is slang for good or fashionable.
「cool」這個詞是「好」或「時髦」的俚語。

en: Standing straight up; or honest and morally correct.
ex: He was an upright man known for his honesty.
他是個以誠實著稱的正直之人。

en: The right to officially reject a law or decision; or to use this right to stop something.
ex: The president vetoed the new tax bill.
總統否決了新的稅法草案。

en: A state of great confusion, disturbance or uncertainty.
ex: The country was in turmoil after the coup.
政變之後，這個國家陷入混亂。

en: A person who tells a story; or a bank employee who deals with customers' money.
ex: The bank teller counted the money twice.
銀行出納員把錢數了兩遍。

en: An official order or instruction from an authority; or giving orders or guidance.
ex: The company issued a directive banning smoking in the office.
公司發布了禁止在辦公室吸菸的指令。

en: The state of being alone, especially in a peaceful way.
ex: He enjoys the solitude of walking alone in the mountains.
他享受獨自在山裡行走的寧靜。

en: Open refusal to obey or respect authority.
ex: They continued to protest in defiance of the ban.
他們不顧禁令繼續抗議。

en: The gradual gathering of more and more of something over time.
ex: The accumulation of snow blocked the road.
積雪堵住了道路。

en: To find a way to make two different ideas, facts or people agree; or to make someone accept something unpleasant.
ex: It is hard to reconcile these two different views.
很難調和這兩種不同的觀點。

en: The quality of continuing to do something in spite of difficulties; or the fact of continuing to exist.
ex: Her persistence finally paid off when she got the job.
她的鍥而不捨終於得到回報，找到了那份工作。

en: The group of elected representatives that makes the laws of a country, such as the Houses of Parliament in Britain.
ex: Parliament voted to approve the new law.
國會投票批准了這項新法律。

en: A woman who is sexually attracted to other women.
ex: The film tells the story of a lesbian couple.
這部電影講述一對女同志伴侶的故事。

en: Members of a royal family; or a payment made to an author or musician each time their work is sold.
ex: The author receives royalties on every book sold.
作者每賣出一本書就能得到版稅。

en: Relating to a scale of temperature in which water freezes at 32 degrees and boils at 212 degrees.
ex: Water freezes at thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit.
水在華氏三十二度時結冰。

en: A situation in which people or groups compete with each other, often unfriendly.
ex: There is a bitter rivalry between the two football clubs.
這兩家足球俱樂部之間有激烈的對抗。

en: To walk with difficulty because of an injury to a leg or foot; or soft and not stiff.
ex: He limped off the field with an injured ankle.
他腳踝受傷，一瘸一拐地離開球場。

en: So useful or valuable that you cannot measure its worth.
ex: Her advice was invaluable to me when I started the business.
創業之初，她的建議對我極其寶貴。

en: Likely to become something in the future; or expected to happen.
ex: The agent showed the prospective buyers around the house.
仲介帶潛在買家參觀了這棟房子。
